subject: Banks shelve bond sale for Anthropic-tied Texas data center
text:
Source: https://news.bloomberglaw.com/capital-markets/banks-shelve-bond-sale-for-anthropic-tied-texas-data-center (Bloomberg via Bloomberg Law, 28 Oct 2026)

Site Watch summary: Morgan Stanley leads lenders on a $15B loan for the Nexus Data Centers site in Hubbard, Texas, which Anthropic leases. They are delaying a planned $5B-$7B bond sale because Texas paused new data-center projects to review grid risks. The sale may now be spread over the next year, leaving the debt on the banks' balance sheets longer.

Readable with source.mjs: only the opening, "Banks are delaying plans to offload part of a $15 billion loan to fund a data center tied to Anthropic PBC in Texas, after the state put a hold on new projects while assessing risks to its power grid." and "Lenders, led by Morgan Stanley, have already lined up around $15 billion to finance construction of the data center in Hubbard". The $5B-$7B bond size, Nexus and the "spread over the next year" detail are behind the paywall: leave them out unless a readable source gives them. Not the same story as the $63B Broadcom financing (brief 2026-10-27-banks-blackstone-63b-anthropic-compute).
